title: fix(spec): SessionUser.image accepts null, the shape every /auth/* route serves
body:
Fixes #17235

Clause-②: yes — this widens a **published accept set** (`@objectstack/spec`), so the changeset is `minor`. The `needs:contract-review` carrier is the seat's, on both card and PR; this PR neither hangs, strips nor waits on it.

The severity binding was re-read on `origin/main` at `fed4a15ab5`, **`AGENTS.md:1067-1068`**: a `yes` declaration takes at least **`minor`**, it may carry at most one arm from the closed pair `(widening)`/`(narrowing)`, `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, and `no (widening)` is malformed. This diff is a widening, so `minor` is the floor and nothing here is breaking. (An earlier revision cited `AGENTS.md:1043`. That was a real read — but off the **shared checkout** at `7e58d177ee`, AGENTS.md blob `f04446be`, which is not `main` and whose HEAD other agents move. Measured across three refs: the same rule sits at **1043** on that tree and at **1067** on `origin/main`, blob `fb8bae3e` — and this branch's own merge base `bf61f0a196` carries the *same blob as main*, so the worktree would have answered correctly all along. The text was rewritten too, not merely moved. ⇒ A bare `AGENTS.md:NNNN` is a weak citation: nothing in it says which tree it was read against, and the same sentence legitimately has two different line numbers. The ref plus the quoted rule is what makes it checkable.)

Ruled by director batch **#138 item 1**, maintainer verbatim 「138 同意」 — option **A**, pure widening.

## What changed

`SessionUserSchema.image`: `z.string().optional()` becomes `z.string().nullish()`. A string, `null`, or the key absent are all accepted.

better-auth owns the avatar column, stores it nullable, and serialises it present-and-null, so every `/auth/*` session body the platform produces carried a value its own published declaration rejected.

## The widening bites — before / after, measured

`SessionResponseSchema.safeParse` on a session body, varying only `data.user.image`:

| `data.user.image` | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `null` | **FAIL** `data.user.image [invalid_type] Invalid input: expected string, received null` | **pass** |
| `"https://x/a.png"` | pass | pass |
| key ABSENT | pass | pass |
| `42` (number) | FAIL `expected string, received number` | **FAIL** (unchanged) |
| `{}` (object) | FAIL `expected string, received object` | **FAIL** (unchanged) |

Exactly **one** row moved, and it is the ruled one. The failing issue path and message match the card verbatim. Lit control on the instrument: a body with `data.session` removed reports `data.session` in both legs, so the parse really is checking.

`.nullish()`, **not** `.nullable()`: the key's absence is a legal shape today and no producer was ever measured omitting it, so `.nullable()` would have retired a live shape as the price of admitting `null`.

## Ablation — the pins are real, not a cached green

The declaration was reverted to `.optional()`, `@objectstack/spec` **rebuilt**, and the marker confirmed live in the artifact the suite consumes before reading any result:

```
ablation-dist-preflight: marker present in 4 built files
  packages/spec/dist/api/index.js · index.mjs · browser/api/index.js · index.mjs
ABLATED_TEST_EXIT=1 -> Test Files 2 failed | Tests 5 failed | 17 passed (22)
  expected [ 'data.user.image' ] to deeply equal []                              x3
  expected [ 'success', 'data.user.image' ] to deeply equal [ 'success' ]
  expected [ 'data.session', 'data.user.image' ] to deeply equal [ 'data.session' ]
```

The 5 reddened assertions are exactly the 5 rows this PR edited; the other 17 were untouched. Restore leg, rebuilt again:

```
ablation-dist-preflight --absent: marker absent from all 216 built files
  tree: working tree clean against HEAD
RESTORED_TEST_EXIT=0 -> Test Files 2 passed | Tests 22 passed (22)
```

## The generated page is a second carrier

`content/docs/references/api/auth.mdx` is generated from the schema, so the source edit and the reference page are **two carriers** and a source-only fix ships the old sentence. `check:docs` caught it on the first push; regenerated with `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec gen:schema && gen:docs`, never hand-edited. `git status --porcelain` after the regeneration listed **exactly one path**, inside `content/docs/references/**`; nothing outside it moved, and `packages/spec/authorable-surface.base.json` did not move. `check:docs` then exits **0** ("223 generated files in sync with packages/spec").

Counts on that page, occurrences rather than lines: the old full row `| **image** | `string` | optional | Avatar URL |` is **0**, the new `string \| null` row is **2**, lit control `Avatar URL` is **2**, dark control `nullish` is **0**.

A deliberately loose probe that stopped before the description column still matched **1** row — and that hit is a **true positive on the row this PR leaves alone**: line 92, under `## RegisterRequest`, still reads `| **image** | `string` | optional |  |`. The published reference now shows the two surfaces side by side carrying different types, which is the `:97` finding confirmed from a generated artifact rather than from reading the source.

## The residue rows went in one stroke, not half each

Both client envelope suites pinned `data.user.image` as an **exhaustive** issue list. All rows in both files moved together:

- `packages/client/src/auth-get-session-envelope.test.ts` — case ① `toEqual(['data.user.image'])` becomes `toEqual([])`, plus its header comment.
- `packages/client/src/auth-login-register-envelope.test.ts` — `const RESIDUE` becomes `[]` (covers `register()` and `login()`), plus **two negative controls** at ③ that carried the residue alongside a deliberately reintroduced defect: `['success','data.user.image']` becomes `['success']`, and `['data.session','data.user.image']` becomes `['data.session']`.

Discriminating counts after the edit: residue inside any `toEqual(...)` expectation is **0** in both files (`grep -z` used, so a wrapped phrase cannot give a false zero), while `toEqual(` itself is still present 1x and 6x respectively — the lists are empty because the residue closed, not because the assertions were deleted. The two surviving `data.user.image` mentions are past-tense comments recording the closure.

The lists stay pinned as exhaustive, so a regression on `success` or `data.session` reddens them instead of hiding inside an already-failing parse.

## Acceptance

「`SessionResponseSchema.safeParse(await client.auth.me())` succeeds for a signed-in user with no avatar on all three `/auth/*` routes」 — met, through a real `AuthManager` over a real `ObjectQL` on a real `SqliteWasmDriver`: `get-session` (case ①), `register()` and `login()` (case ②). 22 passed.

## Acceptance notes

**`auth.zod.ts` carries `image: z.string().optional()` at a second site, and the ruling does not reach it.** The ruling names the declaration at old `:33` (`.describe('Avatar URL')`). The second site — old `:97`, now `:111` — is `RegisterRequestSchema.image`, and it is **deliberately left alone**:

- It sits under the file's own `// Requests` banner, not the `// Responses` one.
- Its producer is the opposite party. `packages/client/src/index.ts:4463` types it as the **input parameter** — `register: async (request: RegisterRequest): Promise pointing at SessionResponse` — so the API **caller** authors it, while `SessionUserSchema` is what better-auth **serves**. `packages/cli/src/commands/register.ts:128` constructs that payload by hand and does not set `image` at all.
- Nothing in this card measures a registration caller sending `null`. Widening an input surface would be a separate published accept-set change with its own Clause-② weight, and it is unruled.

So 「the one declaration」 means one of the two, not both. Noted, not filed — there is no measured defect here, and no in-flight PR or person is carrying this file otherwise.

**The claim's 工作项面 reading was incomplete** (reported, not a defect): it listed residue at `auth-login-register-envelope.test.ts` :33, :39, :310-312, but live assertion rows also sat at :319 (`const RESIDUE`), :346 and :362 (the two negative controls). Removing only the listed rows would have left the suite red.
